Reframing the September 18, 2019 FOMC statement through the Beige Book points to modest but positive momentum with notable cross-currents. Districts reported continued employment gains and tight labor markets, with wage pressures especially for low-skill and construction positions. Consumer spending and nonfinancial services were generally positive, commercial real estate activity was steady with some pickup in leasing, and lending volumes grew modestly. Offsetting these strengths, contacts widely cited tariff and trade-policy uncertainty; transportation activity softened in some areas tied to global demand; home sales were constrained and new construction flat; and agricultural conditions remained weak due to weather, commodity prices, and trade-related uncertainties. This mix broadly validates the FOMC’s “moderate growth/strong labor market” characterization while acknowledging sector-specific softness and external headwinds. Compared with a SLOOS-only lens, the Beige Book is somewhat more constructive given steady CRE and modest lending growth, so the overall tone is slightly firmer but still cautious.
